sections.h2: What the Warren County Clerk does for a home seller
sections.html:
When a Bowling Green house changes hands, the deed ends up in this office. The clerk handles elections, motor vehicles and public land records, plus marriage licenses, notary commissions and delinquent property taxes.

  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102.
  • Phone: (270) 842-9416. The fax for legal recordings is (270) 843-5319.
  • Doors open weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm.
  • The deed room is on the building's bottom floor, with public terminals and a deputy records clerk on hand to get you started.

Some errands belong elsewhere. Driver's licenses come from the state Transportation Cabinet, and traffic citations go to the Circuit Clerk at 1001 Center St., Suite 102.

sections.h2: Which county records a Kentucky deed?
sections.html: The clerk where the land sits, or where most of a split parcel sits. That rule comes from KRS 382.110, which also bars a clerk from taking a deed that skips the seller's source of title. When the seller bought by a recorded deed, the new one cites that earlier deed's book, page and recording date. An heir states how and from whom the property came. A lender taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure has 45 days to file it.

sections.h2: What a deed must say before Warren County will file it
sections.html:
The contents come from KRS 382.135, and a deed lacking any item is refused. A deed from a title attorney normally covers all of them.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for the grantor and grantee.
  • The whole consideration paid.
  • A forwarding address for the tax bill of the year of transfer.
  • A sworn, notarized statement signed by both parties that the price on the deed is the whole price. A gift instead needs a statement saying so and estimating fair cash value.

When a house passes through an estate, the personal representative files a separate affidavit in every county with estate land, naming who gets what and its value. Clerk staff cannot do a title search or answer whether liens exist, so leave that to a title company.

For most documents a charge of $3.00 applies to each page beyond five. Mortgages and releases of mortgage work differently, adding $5.00 for each page beyond thirty.

Selected Warren County recording fees

Deed$50

Copies are cheaper: $.50 a page from a public terminal, $5 for a certified copy of up to three pages with $.50 for each more, and $3 for a big plat. Call before you mail a package to get the exact total.

The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 of value, rounding any remainder up. KRS 142.050 makes the clerk do the math and take payment before accepting the deed. The clerk's cut is 5 percent, and the treasurer gets the remainder every quarter.

Value means the whole price including liens, or the estimated open market price for a gift. The statute exempts many ordinary transfers, such as foreclosure deeds, deeds that grant or release security for a debt, divorce transfers between spouses, partitions, tax sales, and nominal price deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild. Match your deed to the statute's wording before counting on an exemption.

sections.h2: How to look up land records
sections.html:
Two routes exist. You can sit at a terminal in the deed room, or you can use eCCLIX, a subscription service from a records vendor. Personal users get five free searches a day, and commercial users pay a subscription. Because the index follows party names and document types, an address search will not work. Look the owner up on the PVA's site first, then search the clerk's records by name.

Staff will point out how the system works but will not run the search for you. DocAlert is another service the clerk promotes. It is free and emails you when a mortgage or deed is filed under your name, which helps owners of vacant rentals or land spot fraud.

Four vendors accept electronic recordings:

  • Simplifile, (800) 460-5657
  • CSC, (866) 652-0111
  • ePN, (888) 325-3365
  • Hopdox, (385) 501-5103 ext. 010

After April 15 the sheriff's open bills belong to the clerk. The office takes payments until its annual sale, runs a current list in PDF, and takes buyer registrations for the sale held at its East 10th Avenue office. Most outside buyers must also register with the state first, so the clerk sends them to the Department of Revenue's form. Call for a payoff before closing, because interest and commissions keep growing each month and the lien can travel with the land for 11 years.

Work done without a permit is where closings tend to snag. Warren County's Division for Building Services at 1141 State Street handles permits outside Bowling Green and Oakland and states that all new construction needs one. Sheds starting at 120 square feet, decks and pools need permits too, and the county's stormwater office generally bars fences, sheds, pools and additions inside a drainage easement without a written exception. Bowling Green has its own inspector at (270) 393-3615.

A farm with a long chain of title may have early records in Logan County rather than here, so ask the deed room where to look. Renters occupy 44.4 percent of homes in the county, and the median rent is $1,002, so many sellers are landlords. The median home value is $258,000.

sections.h2: Selling a house that needs work or owes tax
sections.html:
A tenant, a probate delay, half finished repairs or unpaid taxes need not hold up a sale, since a cash buyer will purchase as is. Line up the paperwork first: a payoff from the clerk for any delinquent bill, the sheriff's figure for the current year, and permit sign-offs for any work done on the house. Hand these to the closing attorney so the deed, the transfer tax and the payoffs all settle on one day.

Confirm that the deed you plan to sign cites how you took title and carries the mailing addresses and price statement described above. A deed that the clerk refuses can delay the closing, and a second trip to the recording counter costs time even when the fee is small.

Bring photo ID to the closing, and ask the closing attorney to confirm the clerk's current fee total before the day.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded in Warren County?
faqs.a: At the Warren County Clerk's office, reached by mail at P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, or by phone at (270) 842-9416. Four e-recording vendors also send documents electronically.

faqs.q: How much does Warren County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The base fee is $50, with $3.00 added for each page past the fifth. A deed of correction costs $46. Transfer tax is extra, and the seller covers it.

faqs.q: Can I find a Warren County deed using only the address?
faqs.a: No. The clerk indexes by party names and document types. Find the owner by address on the PVA's website first, then search the clerk's index under that name.

faqs.q: Will clerk staff check my title?
faqs.a: No. Staff can demonstrate the index, yet they are not permitted to run a title search or declare a property free of liens. Hire a title company or attorney for that.

faqs.q: Who owes Kentucky's transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: It falls on the grantor in the deed, at half a dollar per $500 of value. The clerk collects it first, then records the deed.
